Subject: Dedicated SKU mapping & fractional-burst plan for Starlite AI (proposal)

Hi Alex / Priya —

Quick follow-up from last week’s call. We built a compact proposal that maps Starlite’s mixed workload into a Dedicated pool with a fractional-burst strategy (reserve baseline H100s/A100s where latency-critical, use L4 for high-volume short-text paths). This aims to keep your committed spend lean while protecting the 99th %-tile latency SLO for the embedding/search and chat endpoints.

Key asks:
- Confirm monthly peak QPS profile in the linked sheet (I filled estimated percentiles).
- Decision on whether RLHF training inference should be in scope for reserve vs. burst.

Attached: a short cost model, token-profile scenarios, and a SKU-mapping workbook with suggested slotting and burst gates.

Proposed next steps (45m): review mapping, lock baseline reserve, and agree on burst throttles + fallback policy.

Cheers,
Kim

Subject: Re: Dedicated SKU mapping & fractional-burst plan for Starlite AI (proposal)

Thanks, Kim — this looks useful. A few clarifications before we run the workbook with our telemetry team: 

1) Our traffic is bursty with two peak windows (US mornings and late EU afternoons). Peak concurrency is about 850 short requests/sec (median token length ~18) and 60 long-context chat sessions (avg 1.6k tokens).
2) RLHF inference (reward model scoring) runs at lower volume but is memory-bound due to long contexts; we prefer it to be on H100 if reserved.

Can your plan show a split where RLHF and chat-critical nodes are reserved on H100/A100 and short-request front-line is routed to an L4 pool with autoscaling/burst? Also include estimated cold-start latency for L4 in the burst path.

Alex

Subject: RE: Dedicated SKU mapping & fractional-burst plan for Starlite AI (proposal)

Kim / team —

I updated the workbook with two scenario tabs: 
A) Latency-first reserve: reserve mix = 6x H100 + 8x A100, L4 in burst-only autoscaling group. This keeps 99p chat latency < 220ms for the configured token mix but increases commit by ~28% vs. their current forecast.
B) Cost-lean reserve: reserve mix = 3x H100 + 4x A100 with an L4 pool sized for steady-state short requests and a larger burst lease. Cold-start cost for L4 bursts is ~0.5s extra p99 on first token; subsequent requests reuse warmed slots via prefix cache.

Notes added in workbook: fractional-burst policy (percentile gates), fallback order (A100 -> H100 for memory-heavy if H100 saturated), and slot consolidation heuristics to limit KV-cache eviction during bursts.

Irene, David: flagged two ops risks for confirmation — (~1) inter-GPU migration latency for large KV caches, (~2) reserve capacity hedging if monthly peak shifts >20%.

-Ben

Attachments referenced: starlite-frac-burst-mapping.xlsx (updated)

- Can we get a runbook for the burst scale-down window to avoid premature slot eviction (we saw issues with other vendors)?
- For RLHF scoring on H100, what headroom/overprovision should we commit to for gradual model growth?

Procurement is looping in contract language requests (cc'd). If the runbook and a short SLA appendix for burst behavior look good, we can move to a 30% reserve (trial for 3 months) and DocuSign the amendment.
